Question Choices: Fill: Solve the system $y = 8 - 3x$ and $2x + y = 6$. Find $x$.
Hints: Replace one variable with its equivalent expression, then solve and substitute back.
Solution: System: y=8-3 × x; 2 × x+y=6. Isolate y: y=(-3)x+(8). Substitute into the other equation: (2)x+(1)[(-3)x+(8)]=6. Combine: (-1)x=-2, so x=2. Then y=(-3)(2)+(8)=2. Check both equations: 3(2)+1(2)=8; 2(2)+1(2)=6. Requested answer: 2.

Hints: Use equivalent line equations: identical lines, distinct parallel lines, or one intersection.
Solution: In standard form the first equation has coefficients (4,-2) and right side 12. Multiplying it by 1/2 gives coefficients (2,-1) and right side 6. The second has the same left side and right side 6. The constants agree: the same line, infinitely many solutions. Requested answer: Infinite.

Solution: $13 = 4x - 3$ → $16 = 4x$ → $x = 4$ Reduced equation: 4 × x-3=13. Solving gives x=4; substitution confirms equality. Requested answer: 4.

Hints: Replace one variable with its equivalent expression, then solve and substitute back.
Solution: System: y=6-x; 3 × x-y=10. Isolate y: y=(-1)x+(6). Substitute into the other equation: (3)x+(-1)[(-1)x+(6)]=10. Combine: (4)x=16, so x=4. Then y=(-1)(4)+(6)=2. Check both equations: 1(4)+1(2)=6; 3(4)+-1(2)=10. Requested answer: 4.
